**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The IP regime in Article X does not offend the rule:

- **No assignment of our IP or results to RevMed.** Ownership of Program Inventions follows inventorship (§10.1(a)), with "Sanofi Sole Program Know-How"/Patents (§1.109) staying with us. The only assignment obligations run *to* us or to the engaging party (§10.1(a) third-party invention assignment; §3.5 subcontractor assignment or fallback perpetual, fully-paid, exclusive, royalty-free licence; §6.2 RevMed assigns all Regulatory Approvals, INDs and NDAs to Sanofi).
- **Joint ownership is not walk-away territory.** §10.1(b) is joint ownership *with* an unrestricted right to exploit and license, no duty of accounting and no consent requirement, backed by a nonexclusive, irrevocable, perpetual, fully-paid, worldwide, sublicensable licence for non-US jurisdictions. RevMed's interest is additionally subject to our exclusive licences and its payment obligations — an asymmetry in our favour.
- **Licence-in is broad.** §3.1 grants Sanofi an exclusive (even as to RevMed) licence under all RevMed Licensed Technology, which includes RevMed's undivided half of Joint Program Technology (§1.99).

Noted in the rationale but not flagged: §10.1(a) is materially redacted, so the precise inventorship allocation can't be fully verified, and there is no standalone "Customer Data" ownership sentence — data is instead captured by the Program Inventions/Know-How and regulatory-ownership constructs normal for a collaboration of this type.
